title: Five ideas, one first pilot
scenario:
You manage customer operations at a travel company that sells package holidays. After a workshop, your team sent five ideas for AI. Your boss wants one to look at first and asks you to use the facts, not the loudest voice in the room.

You counted volume and time for each idea from last month's records. The exhibit shows the list.
exhibit:
AI ideas from the workshop (made-up example data)

Idea                               Per month   Time each   Someone waits?  Written rules?
A. Annual strategy deck for board   1 per year  3 weeks     yes             no
B. Turn supplier hotel PDFs into    2,500       12 min      no              yes, fixed
   our standard listing format                               (next day ok)   template
C. Reply to "where is my booking    3,000       2 min       yes             yes
   confirmation" emails
D. Rename files on the shared drive 40          30 sec      no              yes
E. Handle complaints about cancelled 150        25 min      yes             no, case
   holidays and agree compensation                                           by case

questions.prompt: Which idea passes all four signs of good repetition and saves the most staff time per month?

options.text: Idea A, because the board deck is the slowest and hardest task on the whole list.
options.explanation: It happens once a year and has no written rules. Hard, rare work is a poor first target.

options.text: Idea B, because it repeats 2,500 times with a fixed template and written rules.
options.explanation: Right. 2,500 × 12 minutes is about 500 hours a month, with the same input type, a fixed output shape and written rules.

options.text: Idea D, because file renaming is simple and the rules are already written down.
options.explanation: 40 × 30 seconds is 20 minutes a month. It is frequent but tiny, so the saving is small.

options.text: Idea E, because complaints take the longest each time and upset customers.
options.explanation: It is case by case with no written rules for compensation. Without written rules, nobody can test what a good answer is.

questions.prompt: Idea B results are needed by the next day, not right away. What does this mean for running it?

options.text: It should run in a live chat window so staff can watch each listing being written.
options.explanation: Nobody needs each result right away, so watching each one live adds staff time without adding value.

options.text: It must wait until the company can afford a real-time system that answers in seconds.
options.explanation: Speed in seconds is not needed here. The next day is fine, which opens a cheaper option.

options.text: It should use the largest model available, because overnight jobs have no cost limits.
options.explanation: Overnight jobs still cost money per token. OpenAI's model selection page says frequent automations make cost add up faster.

options.text: It fits a batch job, which both vendors price 50% lower than standard requests.
options.explanation: Right. Both batch pages describe a 50% discount for work that doesn't need an immediate response.

questions.prompt: The finance lead says: "2,500 listings a month will cost a fortune." What is the best response?

options.text: Test lighter models on the same hotel PDFs; keep the lightest that meets the quality bar.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's model selection page gives this advice, and Anthropic's model guide lists high-volume, straightforward tasks as a fit for starting with a faster, cheaper model.

options.text: Drop Idea B and pick Idea D instead, because a small task will always cost less to run each month.
options.explanation: Idea D costs little but saves only about 20 minutes a month. Cost only matters next to the value.

options.text: Run Idea B only on 50 listings a month for good, so the cost stays as low as possible.
options.explanation: That keeps the cost low by throwing away most of the saving. A test on samples is useful, but not as the final plan.

options.text: Ignore the concern, because AI costs are too small to matter at this volume.
options.explanation: Volume multiplies spend. OpenAI's page says frequent automations make cost add up faster, so it is worth checking.
